indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of a sequence, so the bark goes inside the run of notes

blocks.note: 10-across is NOTES; here three sol-fa notes, sol, la and re
the sound of a dog's bark, as in comic strips

explanation.surface: A dog barks in the middle of some music and a burst of sunshine, a cheerful jumble of scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: Every 10 in this puzzle stands for the answer to 10-across, NOTES, and the setters use it in several senses; here it is sol-fa syllables: SOL, LA, RE with ARF breaking in.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar flare is a sudden eruption of energy from the sun, which the question mark admits is a whimsical way to describe it.

clue.text: Ridiculous, with no pennies in your ears?

indicators.note: what is in your ears is what you hear, so the spelling follows the spoken sound

blocks.note: with no pennies means without cents, and that is what it sounds like

explanation.surface: Broke, with no coins jingling in your ears, a silly situation.
explanation.walkthrough: A penny is a cent in American money, so having none leaves you cent-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Something senseless lacks all sense, which makes it absurd and ridiculous.

indicators.note: dissonant sounds clash out of harmony, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: two sol-fa notes, la and ti
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Singers' vocal ranges in a few jarring duets.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means freedom or scope, and latitudes are the ranges within which one may act.

clue.text: Lists of chickens with one egg instead of two

indicators.note: instead of means one thing stands in the place of another

blocks.note: roosters are male chickens
an egg is round like the letter O
the two egg-shaped letters already in the word

explanation.surface: Inventories of chickens with one egg where there should be two.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster is a list of names, such as a duty rota or team list.

clue.text: Exhausted source of primal urges? That's clear

blocks.note: limp means drained and exhausted
in Freud, the id is the source of instinctive drives

explanation.surface: A tired psychology student finally gets Freud's idea of the id: that's clear now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's clear' sounds like the end of an explanation; clear is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water or prose is transparent and lucid, which is to say clear.

blocks.note: three sol-fa notes, re, la and ti
an actor appearing in a show is on

explanation.surface: Musical notes appear in a play or film called Mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is one example of a family member, or relation; perhaps marks the example.

clue.text: Use molten rock, flowing upward around island's tip

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter
in a down entry, flowing upward reads the word from bottom to top
around puts the turned word on both sides of the other letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of island
lava is molten rock from a volcano

explanation.surface: On a volcanic island, lava wells up around the tip of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail oneself of something is to make use of it; as a noun, avail means use or benefit.

clue.text: For example, 4 and 6 and 7 (shifting top to bottom)

indicators.note: in a down entry, moving the top letter to the bottom carries the first letter to the end

blocks.note: the number written out as a word

explanation.surface: A list of numbers, with something shifting from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like references to other clues, but they are just numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Four and six are even numbers, which in a plural noun sense are evens.

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: big means large
a stake is a bet

explanation.surface: The gallows is a large stake set upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' suggests a wooden post that fits a scaffold, but it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet is a gallows, or an upright post on which bodies were hung after execution.

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect means reading the phrase from its end to its start

blocks.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: Looking back, a critic attacks somebody's sales pitches.
explanation.walkthrough: This answer is the 10 that recurs through the puzzle: wherever a clue says 10, read NOTES in one of its senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical note is a sound of a particular pitch, so pitches are notes.

clue.text: 10 children finally riding hybrid in kind of highway

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it
riding in a vehicle puts the riders inside it, so these pieces go within the hybrid

blocks.note: two sol-fa notes, ti and la
the last letter of children
a mule is the hybrid offspring of a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: Kids ride along in a hybrid car on a big highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hybrid' looks like a car the children are riding in, but it is the animal: MUL(TI LA N)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A multilane highway has several lanes running in each direction, one type of road.

indicators.note: something immersed is sunk inside a liquid, so it sits within the other letters
subversive suggests overturning order, so the letters of the following word are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
two sol-fa notes, re and mi

explanation.surface: A radical extremist is absorbed in reading subversive writings.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds the most radical views, beyond the ordinary radical position.

blocks.note: first meaning: 10 is NOTES, here banknotes
second meaning: the projecting brims of caps

explanation.walkthrough: After all the musical notes, this 10 switches to money: paper notes are bills in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill is the American word for a banknote and also for the peak or brim of a cap.

indicators.note: something hurt painfully is knocked out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something like this got painfully crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the long dash printed in the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The long punctuation stroke in the clue, as wide as the letter M, is the em dash.

indicators.note: going berserk is running wild out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers stumble as army units run amok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trips' reads as stumbling, but it means excursions.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings are short excursions or jaunts, just as trips are.

clue.text: Former queen in Norwegian capital: free, footloose and 10

indicators.note: a capital is a word's capital letter, its first
footloose means free to wander, so these letters drift into a new order

blocks.note: the initial letter of Norwegian
taken as written, then rearranged
two sol-fa notes, ti and ti

explanation.surface: A deposed queen lives in Oslo, free and footloose and fancy-free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norwegian capital' wants to be Oslo; it is just the first letter of Norwegian.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was the royal wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten, an ancient Egyptian queen.

clue.text: Hardest tiles, broken up and reassembled repeatedly

indicators.note: pieces broken and put back together come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; the answer is built from these five letters alone
the same letters drawn on again, since repeatedly lets a letter be used more than once

explanation.surface: The toughest tiles have been smashed and pieced back together again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter-bank clue: every letter of the answer comes from tiles, and repeatedly lets S, T and E be used again.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard as steel, so the steeliest thing is the hardest.

blocks.note: a fan is a supporter of a team or star
two sol-fa notes, fa and re

explanation.surface: A fan cheers while the band adds some flourishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a short showy burst of trumpets, which musicians also call a flourish.

clue.text: After 10, Pinocchio at times is well-known

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in reading order

blocks.note: two sol-fa notes, fa and mi
Pinocchio's nose grew whenever he told a lie

explanation.surface: After some music, Pinocchio's fibbing is famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something familiar is commonly known and recognised, so well-known fits.

indicators.note: a picture redrawn is made again in a different form, so the letters are set out anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A two-line verse, set out like a title and a byline, about someone called Sean being sketched again.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestina is a strict verse form of six stanzas reusing six end-words.

clue.text: They used to make home deliveries of iodine and glue, for the most part

definitions.text: They used to make home deliveries

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
cement is a glue

explanation.surface: Old-time delivery men brought medicine and glue to the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Before refrigerators, icemen brought blocks of ice to homes for the icebox.

clue.text: British pilots almost took to the air, drawing…

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the Royal Air Force
flew means took to the air

explanation.surface: British airmen nearly took off, sketching as they went; the dots lead into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests sketching, but it means a draw for prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle is a lottery in which tickets are drawn to decide the winners.

clue.text: I glance diabolically, sporting a halo

indicators.note: something done diabolically is done wickedly and wildly, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A devilish sideways look from someone wearing a halo.
explanation.walkthrough: The diabolical indicator sits beside a saintly definition for contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels are pictured wearing halos, so one sporting a halo looks like an angel.

indicators.note: largely means for the greater part, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: raising crops is cultivating them

explanation.surface: Mainly growing grapes to dry into raisins.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a grape that has been dried, one of the commonest dried fruits.

indicators.note: to roll something is to tumble it over, mixing up its order

blocks.note: 10-across is NOTES, here taken as the bare word

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: pilots drawing rock and roll music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock and roll' reads as one musical phrase, but rock is the definition and roll stirs the letters of 10.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone is a piece of rock, and rock in turn names stone as a material.

indicators.note: stewed food is cooked down into a jumble, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stuffed with a bowl of stewed dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sated means having eaten your fill, so satisfied and full.

clue.text: Mountain nymph with nothing to peruse

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O
to peruse is to read

explanation.surface: A mountain spirit with nothing to read.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth an oread is a nymph who lives in the mountains.

clue.text: In between gold and aluminum, flip wig first

indicators.note: flipping a word turns it end over end
between puts one piece in the gap separating two others

blocks.note: taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminum
rug is slang for a toupee or wig

explanation.surface: Someone flips their wig before placing it between the gold and aluminium trophies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In between' looks like a single phrase, but In is a piece on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event is the opening or first one, such as an inaugural voyage.

clue.text: The poles on either side of 10 instruments

indicators.note: pieces placed on either side of something flank it, one before and one after

blocks.note: taken as written
two sol-fa notes, re and mi
N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Poles stand on either side of an orchestra's instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The and the poles sit on either side of the notes; the theremin, fittingly, is played between two antennas.
explanation.definitionFit: A theremin is an electronic musical instrument played by moving the hands near its antennas.

clue.text: Traditional knowledge encompasses one French river

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: lore is knowledge passed down by tradition
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Folk wisdom includes one particular French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing to the Atlantic.

blocks.note: two sol-fa notes, do and do

explanation.walkthrough: The bird is spelt by singing the same note twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is an extinct flightless bird of Mauritius.

indicators.note: acting recklessly means without care, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Late for a meeting, someone races a cart about without care.
explanation.walkthrough: This time 10 means NOTES in the sense of a written record of what was said.
explanation.definitionFit: A transcript is a written record of what was said, just like the notes taken at a meeting.
